what: A simulated layer and its cell count
title: Building cells and summarising them
text: layer 350 points square 1,000 m side. response z 1.5 times predictor , plus smooth spatial field noise; b noise alone. resolution_profile() select_resolution(), defaults, size cells pooled values 4.5 observations per cell, gives 78 cells 350 points. vignette("resolution") explains size ways set count.
code: library(sf) library(spatialkit)  set.seed(11) n  <- 350 xy <- data.frame(x = 5e5 + runif(n, 0, 1000), y = 5e6 + runif(n, 0, 1000)) D  <- as.matrix(dist(xy)) field <- as.numeric(t(chol(exp(-D / 70) + diag(1e-8, n))) %*% rnorm(n)) xy$a  <- rnorm(n) xy$b  <- rnorm(n) xy$z  <- 1.5 * xy$a + field + rnorm(n, sd = 0.3) pts   <- st_as_sf(xy, coords = c("x", "y"), crs = 32632)  prof <- resolution_profile(pts, "z") size <- select_resolution(prof) size$best ## [1] 78

title: Building cells and summarising them
text: build_tessellation() draws four kinds cell. "voronoi" gives one cell per point given, part area nearer point . observations one cell per observation, spread inside cell give standard error. seeds placed get_voronoi_seeds() set count, cells follow observations: small dense, large sparse. "hex" "square" lay grid equal-area cells, clipped boundary, set cell size data . Hexagons put six neighbours cell distance; squares line axes CRS. grid laid whole area can leave cells observation, points cluster. "triangles" returns Delaunay triangulation points. interpolation work adjacency, meant cell summarise . "hex" "square" need boundary lay grid . clip_target_for() returns one polygon tessellate within: bounding box points, widened expand (fraction longer side 1, distance CRS units otherwise). Passing polygon every method makes tessellations cover ground.  Asked count, hex grid builds 85 cells, 7 observation, square grid 81, 4 empty, 78 Voronoi cells k-means seeds none empty. points drawn uniformly square; clustered points grids leave cells empty. ?build_tessellation gives rules method follows.
code: bnd   <- clip_target_for(pts, expand = 0.02, quiet = TRUE) seeds <- get_voronoi_seeds(n = size, sample_points = pts)  vor <- build_tessellation(seeds, boundary = bnd, method = "voronoi",                           quiet = TRUE) hex <- build_tessellation(pts, boundary = bnd, method = "hex",                           approx_n_cells = size, quiet = TRUE) sq  <- build_tessellation(pts, boundary = bnd, method = "square",                           approx_n_cells = size, quiet = TRUE)  c(voronoi = nrow(vor$cells), hex = nrow(hex$cells), square = nrow(sq$cells)) ## voronoi     hex  square  ##      78      85      81 library(ggplot2)  ggplot(three) +   geom_sf(aes(fill = n), colour = "white", linewidth = 0.2) +   facet_wrap(~ method) +   scale_fill_viridis_c(name = "points\nin cell", na.value = "grey85") +   theme_void()

title: Building cells and summarising them
text: get_voronoi_seeds() places seeds three ways. method = "kmeans", default, takes centres k-means partition sample_points; "random" draws seeds uniformly inside boundary; "provided" takes seeds pass. Given result select_resolution() n, , k-means method returns centres partition profile scored, Voronoi cells cells criteria judged nothing drawn random. Given number, runs new k-means. default partition = "density" point weighted local density, gives many small cells points dense large ones sparse. draws come session’s random-number stream: call set.seed() first, pass set_seed, get seeds . k-means, n upper bound, check nrow() result. seeds carry hull sample_points cover, build_tessellation(seeds) without boundary still makes cells hold every observation. seeds select_resolution() also carry record count set, cells assigned rows keep (see “Pooled values warnings” ).

title: Building cells and summarising them
text: assign_features_to_polygons() takes polygons well points. largest = TRUE, default, polygon goes cell overlaps , result one row per polygon. example groups North Carolina’s counties, ship sf, hexagonal cells laid state outline. 100 counties come back 100 rows, spread 12 cells, 1 14 counties . sf::st_join() layers returns 159 rows, one county cell touch overlap, count per cell taken counts county every cell reaches.
code: nc <- st_read(system.file("shape/nc.shp", package = "sf"), quiet = TRUE) counties <- ensure_projected(nc[, c("NAME", "BIR74", "SID74")]) state    <- st_union(counties) nc_cells <- build_tessellation(coerce_to_points(counties), boundary = state,                                method = "hex", approx_n_cells = 12,                                quiet = TRUE)$cells  grouped <- assign_features_to_polygons(counties, nc_cells,                                        polygon_id_col = "cell_id") joined  <- st_join(counties, nc_cells)  c(counties = nrow(counties), grouped = nrow(grouped), joined = nrow(joined)) ## counties  grouped   joined  ##      100      100      159 ggplot() +   geom_sf(data = grouped, aes(fill = cell), colour = "grey40",           linewidth = 0.1) +   geom_sf(data = nc_cells, fill = NA, colour = "black", linewidth = 0.5) +   scale_fill_manual(values = grDevices::hcl.colors(nlevels(grouped$cell),                                                    "Set 3"),                     guide = "none") +   theme_void()

title: Building cells and summarising them
text: summarize_by_cell() reduces assigned rows one row per cell. Passing cells_sf attaches cells’ geometry, result maps, keeps cells hold observation. columns, order: cell_id, n, observations cell. cell none n = NA, stays result, map shows data. resp_mean_z, plain mean response. predictor_vars, predictor gets pred_mean_<name> columns kinds . ..sd_resp_z ..se_resp_z, standard deviation inside cell standard error mean. cell one observation standard error NA. cell_weight, cell’s effective sample size: count non-missing responses, divided design effect deff applies one. Pass weights regression cell values. ..pooled_resp_z, pooled value: cell’s mean pulled toward mean observations 8 nearest cells (nearest centroid observations). mean cell’s target, ..pooled_target_resp_z. cell’s weight, ..pooled_w_resp_z, share pooled value cell’s mean, grows cell’s count. estimate = "mean" leaves three columns . plain mean pooled value estimate cell’s true mean: expected value one observation located cell way observations . Neither average surface cell’s area. Pooled values maps predicting observations. regression cell values use plain means cell_weight; ..pooled_w_resp_z regression weight. arguments add columns. deff 1 adds deff_applied deff_method, area = TRUE adds cell_area n_per_area, conf_level adds confidence interval mean (..ci_lo_*, ..ci_hi_*), obs_level adds range one observation cell around pooled value (..obs_lo_*, ..obs_hi_*). Away observations interval calibrated. vignette("reporting") says interval answers question, ?summarize_by_cell lists columns “Output columns” “Value”.

what: Standard errors and the design effect
title: Building cells and summarising them
text: naive standard error cell mean, s/\sqrt{n}, treats points cell independent. estimate population (grand) mean, cell mean autocorrelated field varies : points cell share cell’s departure population mean, carry less information count. design effect many times larger cell mean’s variance s^2/n says, n/\text{deff} effective sample size. design effect estimated data ("kish" "variogram") also corrects s, correlation biases low, standard error comes \sqrt{\text{deff}} times naive one; “Standard errors design effects” ?summarize_by_cell gives formula. Leave deff = 1 cell means describe cells, map regression cell values, points spread cell. Set deff cell means feed claim whole population. Kish’s design effect, 1 + (n - 1)\rho \rho intra-class correlation inside cell, grows count cell, section uses bigger cells, square grid asked 24. summarize_by_cell() takes design effect deff. Three settings cells: Across cells standard error median 1.96 times naive one kish 2.35 times variogram. estimate population mean, confidence interval built naive standard error 43 percent width variogram correction gives field. cell’s mean naive standard error better two, close right points spread cell; next section (kriging_adequacy()) measures close field. deff = "kish" estimates intra-class correlation variance within cells applies Kish’s factor. deff = "variogram" takes correlation fitted variogram, uses spatial structure cell labels. usable variogram exists, request falls back "kish" warning class spatialkit_deff_fallback, deff_method column names correction row carries. result records correction per-cell design effects, Kish result intra-class correlation used: cell whose design effect reaches count holds one observation’s worth information, standard deviation says nothing spread standard error NA. Use bigger cells collect points.

Median    Mean 3rd Qu.    Max.  ##   2.531   3.487   4.120   4.143   4.756   5.416 attr(kish, "icc")$resp ## [1] 0.1692353

code: lm_fit <- function(train_sf, response_var = "z", predictor_vars = c("a", "b")) {   d   <- st_drop_geometry(train_sf)   # With no predictors the model is intercept-only: "z ~ 1", not "z ~ ".   rhs <- if (length(predictor_vars)) paste(predictor_vars, collapse = " + ") else "1"   fml <- as.formula(paste(response_var, "~", rhs))   new_spatial_fit(     subclass       = "lm_fit",     engine         = lm(fml, data = d),     formula        = fml,     response_var   = response_var,     predictor_vars = predictor_vars,     data_sf        = train_sf   ) } predict.lm_fit <- function(object, newdata = NULL, ...) {   if (is.null(newdata)) return(fitted(object$engine))   as.numeric(predict(object$engine, newdata = st_drop_geometry(newdata))) } residuals.lm_fit <- function(object, ...) residuals(object$engine) fitted.lm_fit    <- function(object, ...) fitted(object$engine) # Registered so that spatialkit's own calls find the methods wherever this # code runs; at the top level of a script they are found without it. for (g in c("predict", "residuals", "fitted"))   registerS3method(g, "lm_fit", get(paste0(g, ".lm_fit")))  fit <- lm_fit(pts) fit ## <lm_fit> spatial model fit ##   Formula : z ~ a + b ##   n       : 350 ##   CRS     : EPSG:32632

code: hull <- clip_target_for(pts, expand = 0.02, quiet = TRUE) grid <- create_grid_polygons(hull, target_cells = 200, type = "square") gp   <- suppressWarnings(st_centroid(grid)) set.seed(2) gp$a <- rnorm(nrow(gp)) gp$b <- rnorm(nrow(gp), mean = 3)     # centred three standard deviations above the training mean gp$a[1] <- NA                         # one missing predictor value  surface <- predict_surface(gwr, grid = gp) aoa <- area_of_applicability(gp, model = gwr, folds = folds) aoa ## Area of applicability (Meyer & Pebesma 2021) ##  ##   predictors  : 2 (a, b) ##   weighted    : no (all predictors count equally: the model carries no variable importance) ##   training    : 350 points ##   reference   : nearest point outside each of 4 CV folds (block_kfold) ##   normaliser  : 1.7610 (mean pairwise distance) ##   threshold   : 0.1925 (outlier-removed max of training DI) ##   location    : measured on its own; threshold 0.9232 (471.7 metres from the nearest training point) ##  ##   74 of 225 prediction points inside the AOA (32.9%) ##   150 outside: 150 on the predictors, 0 on location (a point can be both) ##   1 not classified (a predictor or the location is missing) ##  ## Predictions outside the AOA are extrapolations; the cross-validated ## performance estimate does not cover them. plot(aoa) inside <- aoa$aoa$AOA %in% TRUE c(inside = sum(inside), outside = aoa$n_outside, unknown = aoa$n_na) ##  inside outside unknown  ##      74     150       1 surface$.pred[!inside] <- NA round(100 * mean(!inside), 1)    # percent of locations masked ## [1] 67.1 ggplot2::ggplot(surface) +   ggplot2::geom_sf(ggplot2::aes(colour = .pred), size = 2) +   ggplot2::scale_colour_viridis_c(name = "predicted z", na.value = "grey75") +   ggplot2::theme_void()

code: set.seed(42) xy    <- st_coordinates(centres) D     <- as.matrix(dist(xy)) field <- as.numeric(t(chol(exp(-D / 120e3) + diag(1e-8, nrow(D)))) %*%                       rnorm(nrow(D)))  pts <- centres pts$elev <- rnorm(nrow(pts)) pts$z    <- 0.8 * pts$elev + 2 * field + rnorm(nrow(pts), sd = 0.3) trend_fit <- function(train_sf, ...) {   d  <- st_drop_geometry(train_sf)   co <- st_coordinates(train_sf)   d$x <- co[, 1]; d$y <- co[, 2]   new_spatial_fit(subclass = "trend_fit",                   engine = stats::lm(z ~ elev + x + y, data = d),                   formula = z ~ elev + x + y, response_var = "z",                   predictor_vars = "elev", data_sf = train_sf) } predict.trend_fit <- function(object, newdata = NULL, ...) {   if (is.null(newdata)) return(stats::fitted(object$engine))   d  <- st_drop_geometry(newdata)   co <- st_coordinates(newdata)   d$x <- co[, 1]; d$y <- co[, 2]   as.numeric(stats::predict(object$engine, newdata = d)) } residuals.trend_fit <- function(object, ...) stats::residuals(object$engine) fitted.trend_fit    <- function(object, ...) stats::fitted(object$engine) # Registered so that spatialkit's own calls find the methods wherever this # code runs; at the top level of a script they are found without it. for (.g in c("predict", "residuals", "fitted"))   registerS3method(.g, "trend_fit", get(paste0(.g, ".trend_fit")))  folds <- make_folds(pts, k = 5, method = "block_kfold", block_size = 100e3,                     seed = 1) cv    <- cv_spatial(pts, "z", "elev", trend_fit, folds = folds) fit   <- trend_fit(pts)

code: library(sf) library(spatialkit)  knn_fit <- function(train_sf, response_var = "z", k = 5L) {   new_spatial_fit(     subclass       = "knnsurf_fit",     engine         = list(xy = st_coordinates(train_sf),                           y = st_drop_geometry(train_sf)[[response_var]],                           k = k),     formula        = as.formula(paste(response_var, "~ 1")),     response_var   = response_var,     predictor_vars = character(0),     data_sf        = train_sf   ) }  predict.knnsurf_fit <- function(object, newdata = NULL, ...) {   e  <- object$engine   xy <- if (is.null(newdata)) e$xy else st_coordinates(newdata)   vapply(seq_len(nrow(xy)), function(i) {     d <- sqrt((e$xy[, 1] - xy[i, 1])^2 + (e$xy[, 2] - xy[i, 2])^2)     mean(e$y[order(d)[seq_len(min(e$k, length(d)))]])   }, numeric(1)) } registerS3method("predict", "knnsurf_fit", predict.knnsurf_fit)  knn_fn <- function(train_sf, ...) knn_fit(train_sf, "z", k = 5L) set.seed(7) n  <- 400 xy <- data.frame(x = 5e5 + runif(n, 0, 1000), y = 5e6 + runif(n, 0, 1000)) D  <- as.matrix(dist(xy)) xy$z <- as.numeric(t(chol(exp(-D / 60) + diag(1e-8, n))) %*% rnorm(n)) +         rnorm(n, sd = 0.3) pts  <- st_as_sf(xy, coords = c("x", "y"), crs = 32632)

code: n_points <- 300  pts_raw    <- st_sample(nc_boundary, size = n_points, type = "random") pts_coords <- st_coordinates(pts_raw) x_coords   <- pts_coords[, 1] y_coords   <- pts_coords[, 2]  elevation <- scale(x_coords)[, 1] * 500 + rnorm(n_points, 3000, 400)  city1 <- c(1530000, 550000)   # near Charlotte in EPSG:2264 city2 <- c(2150000, 750000)   # near Raleigh dist_to_city <- pmin(   sqrt((x_coords - city1[1])^2 + (y_coords - city1[2])^2),   sqrt((x_coords - city2[1])^2 + (y_coords - city2[2])^2) ) pop_density <- pmax(exp(-dist_to_city / 400000) * 5000 + rnorm(n_points, 200, 100), 10)  spatial_field <- 20 * sin(x_coords / 250000) * cos(y_coords / 250000)  y_response <- 50 +   0.01  * elevation +   0.005 * pop_density +   spatial_field +   rnorm(n_points, 0, 5)  points_sf <- st_sf(   y           = y_response,   elevation   = elevation,   pop_density = pop_density,   geometry    = pts_raw ) ggplot() +   geom_sf(data = nc_boundary, fill = "grey95", colour = "black") +   geom_sf(data = points_sf, aes(colour = y), size = 1.1) +   scale_colour_viridis_c(name = "Response (y)") +   theme_void() +   ggtitle("Simulated observations")

code: library(sf) library(spatialkit)  set.seed(42) n  <- 400 xy <- data.frame(x = 5e5 + runif(n, 0, 1000), y = 5e6 + runif(n, 0, 1000)) D  <- as.matrix(dist(xy)) xy$w <- rnorm(n) # Mostly a smooth spatial field (exponential, effective range 3 x 80 = 240 m), # with the weak predictor on top. xy$z <- 0.5 * xy$w +   as.numeric(t(chol(exp(-D / 80) + diag(1e-8, n))) %*% rnorm(n)) +   rnorm(n, sd = 0.3) site <- st_as_sf(xy, coords = c("x", "y"), crs = 32632) size <- select_resolution(resolution_profile(site, "z")) size #> Resolution by size: 89 cells #>   size        : 4.5 rows per cell, the default (obs_per_cell); 400 rows / 89 cells = 4.49 #>   cells       : density-weighted k-means++ starts (power 1, 8 neighbours) #>   estimate    : pooled toward the 8 nearest cells #>   at this size: 0.0% of the rows are alone in their cell; median own weight 0.78 #>   loo         : 0.912 (one cell for the layer: 1.5) #>   note        : the count is set by obs_per_cell = 4.5, the default; no #>                 criterion chose it.  seeds <- get_voronoi_seeds(n = size, sample_points = site) tess  <- build_tessellation(seeds,                             boundary = clip_target_for(site, quiet = TRUE),                             method = "voronoi", quiet = TRUE) asg   <- assign_features_to_polygons(site, tess$cells,                                      polygon_id_col = "cell_id") cells <- summarize_by_cell(asg, "z", id_col = "cell_id", cells_sf = tess$cells)  head(st_drop_geometry(cells)[, c("cell_id", "n", "resp_mean_z", "..se_resp_z",                                  "..pooled_resp_z")], 4) #>   cell_id n resp_mean_z ..se_resp_z ..pooled_resp_z #> 1       1 4   1.3680408   0.3289247       1.0626423 #> 2       2 3  -0.2762594   0.1258383      -0.1086915 #> 3       3 3  -0.9436130   0.5218985      -0.6630103 #> 4       4 5  -1.9008715   0.1581262      -1.4425290 fr <- make_folds(site, k = 5, method = "random_kfold", seed = 1) fb <- make_folds(site, k = 5, method = "block_kfold", block_size = 250,                  seed = 1)  random  <- cv_rf(site, "z", "w", folds = fr, include_coords = TRUE) blocked <- cv_rf(site, "z", "w", folds = fb, include_coords = TRUE)  c(random = random$overall$RMSE, blocked = blocked$overall$RMSE) #>    random   blocked  #> 0.9790119 1.1227029

code: suppressPackageStartupMessages(library(sf)) set.seed(1) n <- 120 train <- st_as_sf(   data.frame(x = 5e5 + runif(n, 0, 1000), y = 5e6 + runif(n, 0, 1000),              a = rnorm(n), b = rnorm(n)),   coords = c("x", "y"), crs = 32632 ) train$z <- 2 * train$a - train$b + rnorm(n, 0, 0.3)  # Prediction points, some of them well outside the training predictor range newpts <- st_as_sf(   data.frame(x = 5e5 + runif(50, 0, 1000), y = 5e6 + runif(50, 0, 1000),              a = c(rnorm(40), rnorm(10, 8)), b = rnorm(50)),   coords = c("x", "y"), crs = 32632 )  res <- area_of_applicability(newpts, train_sf = train,                              predictor_vars = c("a", "b")) res #> Area of applicability (Meyer & Pebesma 2021) #>  #>   predictors  : 2 (a, b) #>   weighted    : no (all predictors count equally: no model was given) #>   training    : 120 points #>   reference   : nearest other training point (no folds supplied) #>   normaliser  : 1.7777 (mean pairwise distance) #>   threshold   : 0.2899 (outlier-removed max of training DI) #>   location    : not measured #>  #>   39 of 50 prediction points inside the AOA (78.0%) #>  #> Predictions outside the AOA are extrapolations; the cross-validated #> performance estimate does not cover them. table(res$aoa$AOA) #>  #> FALSE  TRUE  #>    11    39

code: library(sf) set.seed(1) n <- 400 east  <- runif(n, 0, 1e4) north <- runif(n, 0, 1e4) all_pts <- st_as_sf(   data.frame(x = 5e5 + east, y = 5e6 + north,              income = 30 + 5 * sin(east / 2000) + 5 * cos(north / 1500) +                rnorm(n)),   coords = c("x", "y"), crs = 32632 ) pts    <- all_pts[1:350, ] newpts <- all_pts[351:400, ]  # The count from a size, the cells, the observations in them, the values, # all at the defaults: pooled values at 4.5 observations per cell. prof  <- resolution_profile(pts, "income") sel   <- select_resolution(prof) seeds <- get_voronoi_seeds(method = "kmeans", n = sel, sample_points = pts) tess  <- build_tessellation(seeds, method = "voronoi", quiet = TRUE) asg   <- assign_features_to_polygons(pts, tess$cells, polygon_id_col = "cell_id") out   <- summarize_by_cell(asg, "income", id_col = "cell_id",                            cells_sf = tess$cells, obs_level = 0.90)  # The value at other locations, each placed in the cell of its nearest # seed.  `tess$index` gives the cell of each seed. seeds$cell_id <- tess$index at <- cell_values_at(newpts, out, asg, "income", id_col = "cell_id",                      seeds = seeds) head(at) #>   cell_id    value estimate   obs_lo   obs_hi filled filled_from dist_nearest #> 1      39 28.44976   pooled 25.99484 30.80471  FALSE          NA     238.4435 #> 2       4 37.27735   pooled 34.82244 39.63230  FALSE          NA     115.6546 #> 3      58 23.90035   pooled 21.44544 26.25530  FALSE          NA     271.2353 #> 4      29 38.39229   pooled 35.93738 40.74724  FALSE          NA     367.1291 #> 5      75 21.00320   pooled 18.54829 23.35815  FALSE          NA     227.2415 #> 6      19 34.78451   pooled 32.32960 37.13946  FALSE          NA     351.8853 #>   dist_ratio #> 1  0.9403784 #> 2  0.4561211 #> 3  1.0697034 #> 4  1.4478917 #> 5  0.8961997 #> 6  1.3877727 attr(at, "values_at") #> Cell values at other locations: income, the pooled value #>   cell        : of the nearest seed (the Voronoi cell before its clip to the cover) #>   interval    : 90% for ONE OBSERVATION (obs_lo, obs_hi), centred on the value #>   scored rows : 350 rows at 350 locations, measured in EPSG:32632 #>   spacing     : 253.6, the median distance from a scored location to the #>                 nearest other; dist_ratio is dist_nearest over it #>   filled      : no location #>   count       : 78 cells, set by size (the summary's record, in `count_rule`) #> Away from the observations no interval here is calibrated.  # Without the seeds a location is placed in the polygon that holds it.  One # beyond the layer's edge lies in no polygon: it is filled from the cell of # the nearest observation, and `dist_ratio` says how far that is. beyond <- st_sf(geometry = st_sfc(st_point(c(5e5 + 2e4, 5e6 + 5e3)), crs = 32632)) cell_values_at(rbind(st_sf(geometry = st_geometry(newpts[1:2, ])), beyond),                out, asg, "income", id_col = "cell_id") #>   cell_id    value estimate   obs_lo   obs_hi filled filled_from dist_nearest #> 1      39 28.44976   pooled 25.99484 30.80471  FALSE          NA     238.4435 #> 2       4 37.27735   pooled 34.82244 39.63230  FALSE          NA     115.6546 #> 3      NA 25.39825   pooled 22.94334 27.75320   TRUE          74   10204.7354 #>   dist_ratio #> 1  0.9403784 #> 2  0.4561211 #> 3 40.2456524

title: Compare models on the same cross-validation folds — compare_models_cv
code: library(sf) set.seed(1) n <- 120 dat <- st_as_sf(   data.frame(x = 5e5 + runif(n, 0, 1000), y = 5e6 + runif(n, 0, 1000),              elev = rnorm(n)),   coords = c("x", "y"), crs = 32632 ) dat$price <- 10 + 0.01 * (st_coordinates(dat)[, 1] - 5e5) +   2 * dat$elev + rnorm(n) # The random forest, and GWR beside it when sp is installed, on the same # folds.  "Bayesian" is left out here because a Stan fit per fold takes # minutes; add it to `models` for a run to report. models <- c("RF", if (requireNamespace("sp", quietly = TRUE)) "GWR") cmp <- compare_models_cv(dat, "price", "elev", models = models, k = 3,                          rf_args = list(num_trees = 100),                          gwr_args = list(bandwidth = 30)) #> compare_models_cv(): running CV for GWR ... #> compare_models_cv(): running CV for RF ... cmp$overall[, c("model", "RMSE", "R2", "n_pred")] #>   model     RMSE        R2 n_pred #> 1   GWR 2.281133 0.6738657    120 #> 2    RF 3.711068 0.1368361    120

code: library(sf) set.seed(1) n <- 80 site <- st_as_sf(   data.frame(x = 5e5 + runif(n, 0, 1000), y = 5e6 + runif(n, 0, 1000),              elev = rnorm(n)),   coords = c("x", "y"), crs = 32632 ) site$price <- 10 + 0.01 * (st_coordinates(site)[, 1] - 5e5) +   2 * site$elev + rnorm(n)  # 1. A fit_fn returning a spatial_fit of your own subclass. lm_fit <- function(train_sf) {   new_spatial_fit(     subclass       = "lm_fit",     engine         = lm(price ~ elev, st_drop_geometry(train_sf)),     formula        = price ~ elev,     response_var   = "price",     predictor_vars = "elev",     data_sf        = train_sf   ) }  # 2. The predict() method cv_spatial() scores each fold with. Without it #    every fold fails and `overall` comes back all-NA. predict.lm_fit <- function(object, newdata = NULL, ...) {   if (is.null(newdata)) newdata <- object$data_sf   as.numeric(stats::predict(object$engine, st_drop_geometry(newdata))) } registerS3method("predict", "lm_fit", predict.lm_fit)  cv <- cv_spatial(site, "price", "elev", fit_fn = lm_fit, k = 3, seed = 1) #> cv_spatial(): no folds supplied -- using spatial block k-fold CV (k=3). cv$overall #>       RMSE      MAE     MAPE    SMAPE        R2 Adj_R2 n_pred n_MAPE n_SMAPE #> 1 3.472328 3.009688 21.29953 20.27029 0.2341257     NA     80     80      80 # Compare these before reading the metrics above; fold_status says why # any fold is missing from fold_metrics. c(attempted = cv$n_folds_attempted, succeeded = cv$n_folds_succeeded) #> attempted succeeded  #>         3         3  cv$fold_status #>   fold status message #> 1    1     ok         #> 2    2     ok         #> 3    3     ok          # 3. A metric of your own beside the built-in ones: per fold and pooled. med_ae <- function(y, yhat) c(MedAE = stats::median(abs(y - yhat))) cv2 <- cv_spatial(site, "price", "elev", fit_fn = lm_fit, k = 3, seed = 1,                   metrics = med_ae) #> cv_spatial(): no folds supplied -- using spatial block k-fold CV (k=3). cv2$overall$MedAE #> [1] 2.981173 cv2$fold_metrics[, c("fold", "RMSE", "MedAE")] #>   fold     RMSE    MedAE #> 1    1 3.793601 3.536960 #> 2    2 3.198481 2.590833 #> 3    3 3.359840 2.678648

title: Project an sf object to a CRS suited to its extent — ensure_projected
code: library(sf) pts_ll <- st_as_sf(   data.frame(lon = c(9.1, 9.2), lat = c(48.7, 48.8)),   coords = c("lon", "lat"), crs = 4326 ) # A local extent gets the containing UTM zone; the zone's measured # distance error over the extent travels with the result. st_crs(ensure_projected(pts_ll))$epsg  # 32632 #> [1] 32632 attr(ensure_projected(pts_ll), "crs_choice") #>          name        crs distance_error chosen #> 1 UTM zone 32 EPSG:32632   0.0003984524   TRUE  # A continental extent is scored against the zone and may get an # equal-area projection instead.  The choice is logged with its distance # error and the zone's, not raised as an R warning (see ?spatialkit_quiet); # crs_choice holds every candidate scored. wide <- st_as_sf(   data.frame(lon = c(-120, -70), lat = c(30, 48)),   coords = c("lon", "lat"), crs = 4326 ) wide_p <- ensure_projected(wide) st_crs(wide_p)$proj4string #> [1] "+proj=aea +lat_0=41.729902 +lon_0=-98.42263 +lat_1=33 +lat_2=45 +x_0=0 +y_0=0 +datum=WGS84 +units=m +no_defs" attr(wide_p, "crs_choice")[, c("name", "distance_error", "chosen")] #>                                                      name distance_error chosen #> 1                                             UTM zone 14   0.0175763956  FALSE #> 2   Lambert azimuthal equal-area centred on (-98.4, 41.7)   0.0055662736  FALSE #> 3 Albers equal-area (lat_1=33.0, lat_2=45.0, lon_0=-98.4)   0.0001446928   TRUE  # target_crs overrides the choice. st_crs(ensure_projected(pts_ll, target_crs = 3035))$epsg  # 3035 #> [1] 3035  # For densities per cell the CRS has to be equal-area.  Two candidates are # scored, an Albers conic and a Lambert azimuthal, both centred on the data, # and whichever distorts distance less over the extent is used: here Albers. st_crs(ensure_projected(pts_ll, purpose = "area"))$proj4string #> [1] "+proj=aea +lat_0=48.750011 +lon_0=9.14995 +lat_1=48.716667 +lat_2=48.783333 +x_0=0 +y_0=0 +datum=WGS84 +units=m +no_defs"

code: library(sf) # A Gaussian random field with an exponential covariance: range parameter # 100, so the true effective range is 3 x 100 = 300, plus a small nugget. set.seed(9) n <- 150 xy <- data.frame(x = 5e5 + runif(n, 0, 1000), y = 5e6 + runif(n, 0, 1000)) D  <- as.matrix(dist(xy)) xy$z <- as.numeric(t(chol(exp(-D / 100) + diag(0.1, n))) %*% rnorm(n)) pts <- st_as_sf(xy, coords = c("x", "y"), crs = 32632) r <- estimate_sac_range(pts, response_var = "z") r                            # the effective range, in metres #> 292.1814  #>   directional: 0 deg = 248.1608, 45 deg = 413.7318, 90 deg = 617.9676, #>                135 deg = 426.588  (ratio 2.49) #>   in metres of EPSG:32632; variogram of the response itself attr(r, "directional")       # the four directional ranges #>        0       45       90      135  #> 248.1608 413.7318 617.9676 426.5880  attr(r, "variogram_model")   # the fitted model behind it #>   model    psill    range #> 1   Nug 0.000000  0.00000 #> 2   Exp 1.273642 97.39379 attr(r, "nugget_at_bound")   # TRUE: the fit put the nugget at its bound; #> [1] TRUE                              # ?sac_nugget says how to read that attr(r, "structure_p")       # the test for spatial structure #> [1] 8.510444e-22  # A field whose range the data cannot pin down: the variogram never # reaches a sill within the lags fitted, so the answer is NA, with the # refused value and the reason attached. xy$trend <- sin(xy$x / 400) + rnorm(n, sd = 0.2) r2 <- estimate_sac_range(st_as_sf(xy, coords = c("x", "y"), crs = 32632),                          response_var = "trend") r2 #> NA  #>   directional: 0 deg = 2672.119 (past the fitted lags), #>                45 deg = 2672.119 (past the fitted lags), #>                90 deg = 2672.119 (past the fitted lags), #>                135 deg = 2672.119 (past the fitted lags) #>   in metres of EPSG:32632; variogram of the response itself attr(r2, "rejected_reason") #> [1] "fitted range exceeds the largest lag fitted" attr(r2, "rejected_range") #> [1] 2672.119  # White noise: no structure, so no range. xy$noise <- rnorm(n) r3 <- estimate_sac_range(st_as_sf(xy, coords = c("x", "y"), crs = 32632),                          response_var = "noise") attr(r3, "rejected_reason") #> [1] "no spatial structure detected at the nearest-neighbour scale"

code: if (FALSE) { # \dontrun{ # Not run: fits with Stan, which needs a working C++ toolchain and takes # minutes of sampling. if (requireNamespace("brms", quietly = TRUE)) {   library(sf)   set.seed(1)   n <- 60   dat <- st_as_sf(     data.frame(x = 5e5 + runif(n, 0, 1000), y = 5e6 + runif(n, 0, 1000),                elev = rnorm(n)),     coords = c("x", "y"), crs = 32632   )   dat$price <- 10 + 0.01 * (st_coordinates(dat)[, 1] - 5e5) +     2 * dat$elev + rnorm(n)   # Two short chains keep this to a few minutes; Stan may warn about   # effective sample size, which is the cost of that.  Use its defaults   # (chains = 4, iter = 2000) for a fit to report.   fit <- fit_bayesian_spatial_model(dat, "price", "elev",                                     chains = 2, iter = 1000,                                     compute_loo = FALSE)   print(summary(fit))   head(predict(fit, newdata = dat))    # A zero-inflated count.  The family is the only thing that changes.   # summary()'s R2 and MAPE assume a Gaussian response, so for a count   # read the coefficients here and score the model with cv_bayes(), whose   # CRPS and interval coverage are defined for any response.   dat$count <- rpois(n, exp(0.5 + 0.8 * dat$elev)) * rbinom(n, 1, 0.7)   fit_zip <- fit_bayesian_spatial_model(dat, "count", "elev",                                         family = brms::zero_inflated_poisson(),                                         chains = 2, iter = 1000,                                         compute_loo = FALSE)   coef(fit_zip) } } # }

title: Select GWR predictors by forward selection on AICc — gwr_model_selection
code: library(sf) set.seed(1) n <- 80 dat <- st_as_sf(   data.frame(x = 5e5 + runif(n, 0, 1000), y = 5e6 + runif(n, 0, 1000),              a = rnorm(n), b = rnorm(n), noise = rnorm(n)),   coords = c("x", "y"), crs = 32632 ) # The slope on a rises from 1 in the west to 3 in the east. east <- (st_coordinates(dat)[, 1] - 5e5) / 1000 dat$z <- (1 + 2 * east) * dat$a - dat$b + rnorm(n, 0, 0.3) sel <- gwr_model_selection(dat, "z", c("a", "b", "noise"), bandwidth = 30) sel                     # every model tried, by AICc, with the gaps #> Geographically weighted regression - forward model selection #>  #>   response    : z #>   candidates  : 3 (a, b, noise) #>   observations: 80 #>   models      : 7 #>   bandwidth   : 30 (adaptive; supplied) #>   kernel      : bisquare #>   criterion   : AICc #>  #>  rank n_vars     variables criterion     delta #>     1      2         a + b  70.55026   0.00000 #>     2      3 a + b + noise  81.27942  10.72916 #>     3      1             a 262.02384 191.47358 #>     4      2     a + noise 268.26330 197.71304 #>     5      1             b 371.33475 300.78449 #>     6      0        <none> 374.24430 303.69404 #>     7      1         noise 384.67142 314.12116 #>  #> Selected: z ~ a + b #>  #> No other model is within 2 of the best; the runner-up is 10.73 away. #>  #> The criterion is in-sample and every model shares one bandwidth. #> Confirm with select_features_forward() before relying on this. sel$best                # the winning predictor set #> [1] "a" "b" # Refit with the bandwidth chosen afresh for the selected set. fit_gwr_model(dat, "z", sel$best) #> <GWR> spatial model fit #>   Formula : z ~ a + b #>   n       : 80 #>   CRS     : EPSG:32632 #>   Bandwidth: 35 neighbours (adaptive, bisquare kernel) #>   AICc    : 70.30 #>   Eff. parameters: 22.0 of 80 observations

title: Check whether block kriging would improve cell means — kriging_adequacy
code: library(sf) set.seed(1) n <- 200 x <- 5e5 + runif(n, 0, 1000); y <- 5e6 + runif(n, 0, 1000) d <- as.matrix(dist(cbind(x, y))) z <- as.numeric(t(chol(0.8 * exp(-d / 100) + diag(0.2, n))) %*% rnorm(n)) pts <- st_as_sf(data.frame(x = x, y = y, z = z), coords = c("x", "y"), crs = 32632) bnd <- st_sf(geometry = st_as_sfc(st_bbox(pts))) cells <- create_grid_polygons(bnd, target_cells = 16, type = "square") asg <- assign_features_to_polygons(pts, cells) ka <- kriging_adequacy(asg, "z", cells, k = 4) #> Registered S3 method overwritten by 'stars': #>   method                  from #>   st_interpolate_aw.stars sf   print(ka)                   # the report #> Block-kriging adequacy over 20 cells (200 points, nmax 50) #>   variogram: Nug(0.184, 0) + Exp(1.23, 149); sill 1.42, nugget 0.184 (13%), #>     range 445.9 #>   kriging variance / no-data variance of the cell mean (1 = nothing from the #>     data): median 0.062, range 0.032-0.293; 0 cell(s) above 0.5 #>   kr_gain, the share of the plain mean's error variance that kriging removes #>     under this variogram (1 - kr_var / plain_var): median 0.51, range 0.21-0.81 #>     over the 19 cell(s) with points and a kriged estimate #>   kriged minus plain mean, over the standard deviation the variogram gives that #>     difference (sqrt(plain_var - kr_var)): |shift| > 1 in 6 of 19 cell(s), > 2 #>     in 0 (about 6 and 1 when the variogram is right) #>   naive s^2/n below plain_var (the naive standard error is too small if the #>     variogram is right) in 8 of the 16 cell(s) with two or more points; median #>     s^2/n over plain_var 1.00 #>   empty cells: 1 (kriged estimate and variance available for each) #>   blocked CV (block_kfold, 4 folds, 200 points): var of standardised error 0.95 #>     (1 = kriging variance correct; above 1 = understated), mean -0.11, RMSE #>     0.968 # Variance of the standardised errors: about 1 when the variogram is right attr(ka, "cv")$zscore_var #> [1] 0.950956

code: library(sf) set.seed(1) pts <- st_as_sf(   data.frame(x = 5e5 + runif(60, 0, 1000), y = 5e6 + runif(60, 0, 1000),              a = rnorm(60)),   coords = c("x", "y"), crs = 32632 ) # An offset keeps the response away from zero, where MAPE is undefined. pts$z <- 10 + 2 * pts$a + rnorm(60, 0, 0.3) # Fit on 40 rows and keep 20 back, so the second call is out of sample. fit <- fit_rf_model(pts[1:40, ], "z", "a", num_trees = 50, seed = 1) model_metrics(fit)                           # out-of-bag for a forest #>    n     RMSE       MAE     MAPE    SMAPE        R2 Adj_R2 n_MAPE n_SMAPE #> 1 40 0.409009 0.3236812 3.425689 3.390414 0.9541711     NA     40      40 model_metrics(fit, newdata = pts[41:60, ])   # on the 20 held-out rows #>    n      RMSE       MAE    MAPE    SMAPE        R2 Adj_R2 n_MAPE n_SMAPE #> 1 20 0.5080838 0.3836504 3.56621 3.649174 0.9022065     NA     20      20

title: Build a spatial_fit object for a backend of your own — new_spatial_fit
code: library(sf) set.seed(1) n <- 80 site <- st_as_sf(   data.frame(x = 5e5 + runif(n, 0, 1000), y = 5e6 + runif(n, 0, 1000),              elev = rnorm(n)),   coords = c("x", "y"), crs = 32632 ) site$price <- 10 + 0.01 * (st_coordinates(site)[, 1] - 5e5) +   2 * site$elev + rnorm(n)  # A custom backend: an ordinary linear model behind the spatial_fit interface. lm_fit <- function(train_sf) {   new_spatial_fit(     subclass       = "lm_fit",     engine         = lm(price ~ elev, st_drop_geometry(train_sf)),     formula        = price ~ elev,     response_var   = "price",     predictor_vars = "elev",     data_sf        = train_sf   ) }  # Required: cv_spatial() scores each fold through the predict() generic, # which dispatches on the subclass named above. predict.lm_fit <- function(object, newdata = NULL, ...) {   if (is.null(newdata)) newdata <- object$data_sf   as.numeric(stats::predict(object$engine, st_drop_geometry(newdata))) } registerS3method("predict", "lm_fit", predict.lm_fit)  # Required by summary() and model_metrics(): one value per training row. fitted.lm_fit <- function(object, ...) as.numeric(stats::fitted(object$engine)) registerS3method("fitted", "lm_fit", fitted.lm_fit)  summary(lm_fit(site)) #> Summary of <lm_fit> fit (n = 80) #>  #>   Formula: price ~ elev #>  #>   In-sample metrics: #>     RMSE    = 2.8624 #>     MAE     = 2.4374 #>     R^2     = 0.2622 #>     SMAPE   = 16.40% cv <- cv_spatial(site, "price", "elev", fit_fn = lm_fit, k = 3, seed = 1) #> cv_spatial(): no folds supplied -- using spatial block k-fold CV (k=3). cv$overall #>       RMSE      MAE     MAPE    SMAPE        R2 Adj_R2 n_pred n_MAPE n_SMAPE #> 1 3.472328 3.009688 21.29953 20.27029 0.2341257     NA     80     80      80 # Check that these two agree before reading the metrics above. c(attempted = cv$n_folds_attempted, succeeded = cv$n_folds_succeeded) #> attempted succeeded  #>         3         3

code: # Works on any spatial_fit; a forest keeps the example free of the optional # GWR and Stan backends. library(sf) # price depends on elevation, which the forest sees, and on a spatially # correlated field it does not: that field is what the residual plots are # there to find. set.seed(2) n <- 120 xy <- data.frame(x = 5e5 + runif(n, 0, 1000), y = 5e6 + runif(n, 0, 1000),                  elev = rnorm(n)) D  <- as.matrix(dist(xy[, c("x", "y")])) xy$price <- 10 + 2 * xy$elev +   as.numeric(t(chol(exp(-D / 100) + diag(0.3, n))) %*% rnorm(n)) pts <- st_as_sf(xy, coords = c("x", "y"), crs = 32632) fit <- fit_rf_model(pts, "price", "elev", num_trees = 100, seed = 1) plot(fit, type = "residuals")            # structure left in the residuals  plot(fit, type = "observed_predicted")  if (requireNamespace("gstat", quietly = TRUE))   plot(fit, type = "variogram")          # residual and response variograms

title: Print a residual Moran's I result — print.morans_i
code: library(sf) set.seed(1) dat <- st_as_sf(   data.frame(x = 5e5 + runif(80, 0, 1000), y = 5e6 + runif(80, 0, 1000),              elev = rnorm(80)),   coords = c("x", "y"), crs = 32632 ) dat$price <- 10 + 2 * dat$elev + rnorm(80) fit <- fit_rf_model(dat, "price", "elev", num_trees = 100, seed = 1) print(residual_morans_i(fit)) #> Residual Moran's I = 0.0313   (E[I] = -0.0127, sd = 0.0494) #>   z = 0.891, p = 0.373 #>   null: randomisation moments, approximate for these residuals; n = 80, df = 79 #>   residual kurtosis 2.584 (3 = Gaussian) #>   weights: 80 x 80 dgCMatrix, 8 neighbour(s) per row; not retained, keep_weights = TRUE to keep it

title: Test the residuals of a fitted model for spatial autocorrelation — residual_morans_i
code: # Works on any spatial_fit; a forest keeps the example free of the # optional GWR and Stan backends. library(sf) set.seed(1) n <- 120 dat <- st_as_sf(   data.frame(x = 5e5 + runif(n, 0, 1000), y = 5e6 + runif(n, 0, 1000),              elev = rnorm(n)),   coords = c("x", "y"), crs = 32632 ) # An east-west trend the predictor cannot explain. dat$price <- 10 + 0.02 * (st_coordinates(dat)[, 1] - 5e5) +   2 * dat$elev + rnorm(n) fit <- fit_rf_model(dat, "price", "elev", num_trees = 100, seed = 1) # A large positive I and z: the residuals carry the east-west trend the # forest could not see.  A z near 0 with a large p-value would mean no # structure was left. residual_morans_i(fit) #> Residual Moran's I = 0.6437   (E[I] = -0.0084, sd = 0.0419) #>   z = 15.548, p = 1.653e-54 #>   null: randomisation moments, approximate for these residuals; n = 120, df = 119 #>   residual kurtosis 2.371 (3 = Gaussian) #>   weights: 120 x 120 dgCMatrix, 8 neighbour(s) per row; not retained, keep_weights = TRUE to keep it

code: library(sf) set.seed(1) n <- 120 pts <- st_as_sf(   data.frame(x = 5e5 + runif(n, 0, 1000), y = 5e6 + runif(n, 0, 1000),              a = rnorm(n), b = rnorm(n), noise = rnorm(n)),   coords = c("x", "y"), crs = 32632 ) pts$resp <- 3 * pts$a + 2 * pts$b + rnorm(n, 0, 0.3)  # The learner: a GWR with an adaptive bisquare kernel reaching the 30th # nearest training point.  With no variables it is the kernel-weighted # local mean, which is the baseline: a GWR's local intercept beats a # global mean on any smooth response, so the first variable has to beat # the local mean under the same kernel. fit_fn <- function(tr, vars) fit_gwr_model(tr, "resp", vars, bandwidth = 30) sel <- select_features_forward(pts, "resp", c("a", "b", "noise"), fit_fn,                                k = 3, quiet = TRUE) sel$selected #> [1] "a" "b" sel$baseline$type        # "null model": step 1 was tested against it #> [1] "null model" sel$history[sel$history$step <= 1, c("step", "variable", "score", "gain")] #>   step variable    score       gain #> 1    0   <none> 3.523273         NA #> 2    1        a 2.181982 1.34129082 #> 3    1        b 3.477749 0.04552313 #> 4    1    noise 3.487167 0.03610585  # A learner that cannot fit an empty set takes its no-predictor model # through `null_fn`.  Here the same local mean, written as a spatial_fit # of its own with a predict() method, for a learner that insists on a # variable.  Without `null_fn` that sweep would start from the mean of # each training fold. needs_one <- function(tr, vars) {   if (!length(vars)) stop("this learner needs a predictor")   fit_gwr_model(tr, "resp", vars, bandwidth = 30) } local_mean <- function(tr, bandwidth = 30) {   new_spatial_fit("local_mean_fit",                   engine = list(xy = st_coordinates(tr), y = tr$resp,                                 bandwidth = bandwidth),                   formula = resp ~ 1, response_var = "resp",                   predictor_vars = character(0), data_sf = tr) } predict.local_mean_fit <- function(object, newdata = NULL, ...) {   e  <- object$engine   at <- if (is.null(newdata)) e$xy else st_coordinates(newdata)   vapply(seq_len(nrow(at)), function(i) {     d <- sqrt((e$xy[, 1] - at[i, 1])^2 + (e$xy[, 2] - at[i, 2])^2)     h <- sort(d)[min(e$bandwidth, length(d))]  # the kernel's reach here     w <- ifelse(d > h, 0, (1 - d^2 / h^2)^2)   # bisquare weights     sum(w * e$y) / sum(w)   }, numeric(1)) } registerS3method("predict", "local_mean_fit", predict.local_mean_fit) sel2 <- select_features_forward(pts, "resp", c("a", "b", "noise"), needs_one,                                 k = 3, quiet = TRUE, null_fn = local_mean) sel2$baseline$type       # "null_fn" #> [1] "null_fn" all.equal(sel2$baseline$score, sel$baseline$score)  # the same baseline #> [1] TRUE

title: Choose a cell count from a resolution profile — select_resolution
code: library(sf) # An exponential field with range parameter 200 (true effective range # 600 m) on a 1 km square, with a nugget of 0.6 on a unit sill. set.seed(4) n <- 400 xy <- data.frame(x = 5e5 + runif(n, 0, 1000), y = 5e6 + runif(n, 0, 1000)) D  <- as.matrix(dist(xy)) xy$z <- as.numeric(t(chol(exp(-D / 200) + diag(0.6, n))) %*% rnorm(n)) pts <- st_as_sf(xy, coords = c("x", "y"), crs = 32632)  # The default profile is one size scored for pooled values, and the # default criterion, "auto", reads it by that size. select_resolution(resolution_profile(pts, response_var = "z")) #> Resolution by size: 89 cells #>   size        : 4.5 rows per cell, the default (obs_per_cell); 400 rows / 89 cells = 4.49 #>   cells       : density-weighted k-means++ starts (power 1, 8 neighbours) #>   estimate    : pooled toward the 8 nearest cells #>   at this size: 1.0% of the rows are alone in their cell; median own weight 0.40 #>   loo         : 0.903 (one cell for the layer: 1.23) #>   note        : the count is set by obs_per_cell = 4.5, the default; no #>                 criterion chose it.  # A ladder of counts for plain means, read by Mallows' Cp. prof <- resolution_profile(pts, response_var = "z", n_levels = 12,                            estimate = NULL) sel <- select_resolution(prof, criterion = "cp") sel               # the level, and the flat region around it #> Resolution by cp: 19 cells #>   flat region : 19 to 25, 44 (3 of 12 levels) #>   cells       : density-weighted k-means++ starts (power 1, 8 neighbours) sel$flat          # every level within `tol` of the optimum #> [1] 19 25 44 sel$edge          # the bound the optimum sits on; NA when interior #> [1] NA sel$structured    # FALSE when one cell for the layer does as well #> [1] TRUE  # Reliability prefers coarse cells: it is read at or above the floor the # autocorrelation range sets, and the result says in words when the # floor is choosing. rel <- select_resolution(prof, criterion = "reliability") rel #> Resolution by reliability: 4 cells #>   flat region : 4 to 6 (3 of 12 levels) #>   cells       : density-weighted k-means++ starts (power 1, 8 neighbours) #>   note        : the optimum is the range floor (area / range^2); the bound is #>                 choosing, not the criterion. Fewer cells would be wider than #>                 the range and average over more than one patch of the field. rel$at_floor #> [1] TRUE rel$edge #> [1] "the range floor (area / range^2)"

code: library(sf) set.seed(1) n <- 200 east  <- runif(n, 0, 100) north <- runif(n, 0, 100) # A response with spatial structure, so the within-cell ICC is not zero. pts <- st_as_sf(   data.frame(x = 5e5 + east, y = 5e6 + north,              val = 5 + 0.02 * east + 0.02 * north + rnorm(n, sd = 0.5)),   coords = c("x", "y"), crs = 32632 ) bnd <- st_sf(geometry = st_sfc(st_polygon(list(rbind(   c(5e5, 5e6), c(5e5 + 100, 5e6), c(5e5 + 100, 5e6 + 100),   c(5e5, 5e6 + 100), c(5e5, 5e6) ))), crs = 32632)) grid <- create_grid_polygons(bnd, target_cells = 9, type = "square") assigned <- assign_features_to_polygons(pts, grid)  # Nine cells are too few for pooled values (each would be pulled toward # all the other cells), so these summaries report plain means alone: # estimate = "mean". # IID standard errors (default) against the Kish design effect.  The Kish # correction is large here: about 22 points per cell that share the cell's # part of the trend carry far fewer than 22 independent pieces of # information about the cell mean. naive <- summarize_by_cell(assigned, response_var = "val", estimate = "mean") kish  <- summarize_by_cell(assigned, response_var = "val", deff = "kish",                            estimate = "mean") data.frame(n = naive$n,            se_naive = naive$..se_resp_val,            se_kish  = kish$..se_resp_val) #>    n   se_naive   se_kish #> 1 25 0.09706775 0.7210227 #> 2 28 0.11815220 0.9279034 #> 3 25 0.11573069 0.8596517 #> 4 21 0.11556510 0.7881134 #> 5 23 0.13192931 0.9407000 #> 6 21 0.12707224 0.8665880 #> 7 10 0.18215988 0.8673238 #> 8 27 0.09534639 0.7355266 #> 9 20 0.14402822 0.9590654 attr(kish, "deff_applied")   # method, icc_resp, icc_pred, per-cell deff #> $method #> [1] "kish" #>  #> $icc_resp #> [1] 0.6842466 #>  #> $icc_pred #> [1] NA #>  #> $deff #> [1] 17.42192 19.47466 17.42192 14.68493 16.05343 14.68493  7.15822 18.79041 #> [9] 14.00069 #>   # A 95% interval for each cell mean as an estimate of the grand mean, on # the Kish-corrected standard error and n - 1 degrees of freedom. ci <- summarize_by_cell(assigned, response_var = "val", deff = "kish",                         conf_level = 0.95, estimate = "mean") ci[, c("poly_id", "n", "resp_mean_val", "..neff_resp_val", "..df_resp_val",        "..ci_lo_resp_val", "..ci_hi_resp_val")] #> # A tibble: 9 × 7 #>   poly_id     n resp_mean_val ..neff_resp_val ..df_resp_val ..ci_lo_resp_val #>     <int> <int>         <dbl>           <dbl>         <dbl>            <dbl> #> 1       1    25          5.63            1.43            24             4.14 #> 2       2    28          6.30            1.44            27             4.40 #> 3       3    25          6.93            1.43            24             5.16 #> 4       4    21          6.42            1.43            20             4.77 #> 5       5    23          7.11            1.43            22             5.15 #> 6       6    21          7.89            1.43            20             6.09 #> 7       7    10          7.16            1.40             9             5.19 #> 8       8    27          7.77            1.44            26             6.25 #> 9       9    20          8.16            1.43            19             6.15 #> # ℹ 1 more variable: ..ci_hi_resp_val <dbl>  # Pooled values, and a range for one observation: a smooth field plus # noise at 400 points, on an 8 x 8 grid, so that a cell holds about six. set.seed(2) east  <- runif(400, 0, 8000) north <- runif(400, 0, 8000) pts2 <- st_as_sf(   data.frame(x = 5e5 + east, y = 5e6 + north,              val = 10 + 3 * sin(east / 1500) + 3 * cos(north / 1200) +                rnorm(400)),   coords = c("x", "y"), crs = 32632 ) bnd2 <- st_sf(geometry = st_sfc(st_polygon(list(rbind(   c(5e5, 5e6), c(5e5 + 8000, 5e6), c(5e5 + 8000, 5e6 + 8000),   c(5e5, 5e6 + 8000), c(5e5, 5e6) ))), crs = 32632)) grid2 <- create_grid_polygons(bnd2, target_cells = 64, type = "square") assigned2 <- assign_features_to_polygons(pts2, grid2) # estimate = "pooled" is the default. pooled <- summarize_by_cell(assigned2, response_var = "val", obs_level = 0.90) # The plain mean, the pooled value and the weight on the cell's own mean. head(pooled[, c("poly_id", "n", "resp_mean_val", "..pooled_resp_val",                 "..pooled_w_resp_val")]) #> # A tibble: 6 × 5 #>   poly_id     n resp_mean_val ..pooled_resp_val ..pooled_w_resp_val #>     <int> <int>         <dbl>             <dbl>               <dbl> #> 1       1     3          13.6              13.3               0.652 #> 2       2    15          15.0              14.8               0.904 #> 3       3     2          16.6              15.4               0.555 #> 4       4     2          14.0              13.8               0.555 #> 5       5     8          13.4              13.3               0.833 #> 6       6     9          10.9              10.9               0.849 # The range for one further observation in a cell. head(pooled[, c("poly_id", "..obs_lo_resp_val", "..obs_hi_resp_val")]) #> # A tibble: 6 × 3 #>   poly_id ..obs_lo_resp_val ..obs_hi_resp_val #>     <int>             <dbl>             <dbl> #> 1       1             11.3               15.4 #> 2       2             12.8               16.9 #> 3       3             13.4               17.5 #> 4       4             11.8               15.9 #> 5       5             11.3               15.4 #> 6       6              8.86              12.9 attr(pooled, "pooled")   # what was fitted, and what the interval covers #> Cell values: val, 400 rows in 64 cells #>   value       : ..pooled_resp_val, pooled toward the 8 nearest cells (centroids of the rows) #>   variances   : inside cells 1.41 (from 336 values beyond one per cell); #>                 between a cell and its target 0.88 #>   own weight  : median 0.79 (..pooled_w_resp_val) #>   alone       : 0.5% of the rows are the only one in their cell #>   loo         : 1.61 (leave-one-out mean squared error of the pooled value); #>                 one mean for all rows: 10.8 #>   interval    : 90% for ONE OBSERVATION (..obs_lo_resp_val, ..obs_hi_resp_val): #>                 value - 2 to value + 2.09, quantiles of 400 leave-one-out residuals #> Away from the observations no interval here is calibrated.

code: library(sf) # An exponential field with range parameter 200 (true effective range # 600 m) on a 1 km square, with a nugget of 0.6 on a unit sill. set.seed(4) n <- 400 xy <- data.frame(x = 5e5 + runif(n, 0, 1000), y = 5e6 + runif(n, 0, 1000)) D  <- as.matrix(dist(xy)) xy$z <- as.numeric(t(chol(exp(-D / 200) + diag(0.6, n))) %*% rnorm(n)) pts <- st_as_sf(xy, coords = c("x", "y"), crs = 32632) prof <- resolution_profile(pts, response_var = "z", n_levels = 12,                            estimate = NULL)  s <- summary(prof) s #> Resolution picks: 2 criteria over 12 levels (2 to 44 cells) #>  #>   cells: density-weighted k-means++ starts (power 1, 8 neighbours) #>  #>    criterion best  flat region levels in flat region #>           cp   19 19 to 25, 44                     3 #>  reliability    4       4 to 6                     3 #>  #>   reliability: the optimum is the range floor (area / range^2). #>   There the bound is choosing, not the criterion. #>  #>   picks span 4 to 19 cells (4.8x) #>   no level is in every flat region: the criteria disagree over the #>   whole ladder. plot() draws the curves they were read from. attr(s, "common")   # the levels every flat region accepts, if any #> integer(0) attr(s, "bands")    # each criterion's flat region in full #> $cp #> [1] 19 25 44 #>  #> $reliability #> [1] 4 5 6 #>
